role: Method development after prior method failures; not preregistered biological inference or rescue of any existing decision.
question: Does retaining uncertainty about species responses and learning a shared unoriented environmental axis from training species improve held-out species/region prediction against independently structured species, without knowing true response parameters?

geometry.source: Same checksum-verified coordinate-only export, fixed classifiability mask, frozen 184/185 disjoint species assignment, four longitude sectors and 500 km complete-coordinate buffer as actual-support v1.
geometry.sampling: Each fresh replicate draws 20 training and 20 evaluation species per fold, then 20 retained photos each. No replacement within a draw. One priority per original photo. Reuse identical schedules across all scenarios and models; keep all four folds with equal weight.
geometry.mask_caveat: The classifiability mask is measurement-derived selection, not random missingness. No real colour values or real climate are read.

synthetic_worlds.representation: Unchanged two-dimensional fourth-harmonic artificial environment on actual photo coordinates.
synthetic_worlds.generator: Unchanged amplitude*species_sign*tanh(projection/0.5)+N(0,1)>0. One direction and sign per species and one noise per original photo in a global world; reuse across all folds and models. Shared subsets of round(369*f) species chosen before labels; remaining axes independent.
synthetic_worlds.nuisance_arms: No structure at amplitude 0; geographic_specific, environmental_specific and mixed_specific at each amplitude 0.5, 1, 2 (10 arms).

likelihood_models.axis_grid: 48 equally spaced axes theta=k*pi/48, k=0..47; sign integrated per whole species, not per photo.
likelihood_models.saturating_probit: p=Phi(a*tanh(x dot u_theta/0.5)); uniform amplitude grid [0,0.5,1,2]. This knows the simulator's link family and fixed origin, but not true species axes, signs or strengths. It is simulator-informed, NOT an oracle fitted using true response parameters.
likelihood_models.linear_logit: p=logistic(a*x dot u_theta); uniform slope grid [0,0.5,1,2,4,8]. Fixed zero intercept; a deliberately misspecified alternative to the saturating probit generator.
likelihood_models.species_likelihood: For each axis, integrate amplitude/slope and one whole-species sign using log-sum-exp. Normalize by the uniform-axis marginal likelihood to obtain R_s(theta). All 20 labels, including constant-colour samples, enter; no <4-photo class exclusion in likelihood models.
likelihood_models.independent_baseline: Each species has its own independent uniform axis, with the same link/sign/strength prior as the shared alternative. It is not an unstructured label-shuffle baseline.

predictors.joint_train: Uniform prior on f in [0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1] and on theta. Use only training species to form posterior proportional to product_s[(1-f)+f*R_s(theta)]. Score each evaluation species with log(sum_theta,f posterior_train(theta,f)*[(1-f)+f*R_t(theta)]). Average over 20 target species, divide by 20 photos, then mean all four folds. Target labels never update the training posterior. Score is marginal per-target predictive log-density gain, not joint evidence over repeated folds.
predictors.single_source_average: For each training species separately normalize R_s over axes, then average the 20 axis posteriors. Evaluate log of its weighted average of R_t, per target/photo/fold. A predeclared uncertainty-aware individual-source comparator; no shared-fraction parameter is fitted.
predictors.qda_equal: Unchanged original equal-prior Gaussian/QDA and equal source weights, original >=4-per-colour validity rule and ARI score. Same fresh worlds, not copied old counts.
predictors.noncausal_comparison: Comparisons change likelihood family, aggregation and/or score. Improvements cannot be attributed to pooling alone. New likelihood scores and ARI have different units. No outcome-based winner selection.

calibration.rule: Per design use maximum empirical 97.5th percentile (method=higher) over all ten calibration nuisance arms and strengths. Strict score > threshold. Same cutoff for every evaluation arm; never select a known-strength cutoff.
calibration.report: All five designs and all 14 evaluation arms, Wilson 95% intervals and paired detection differences. Intervals condition on estimated thresholds and finite nuisance family. No joint five-design or universal 5% type-I guarantee.
calibration.primary_candidate: linear_logit_joint_train is the deployable-family candidate; saturating_probit is a generator-informed diagnostic. Neither opens real-colour inference by itself.

outputs: all 30000 score records with four fold scores
all 70 evaluation decision counts and Wilson intervals
unit tests and independent scalar probability checks
forbidden: reading biological colours or real climate
using true species response parameters in a predictor
changing seeds, grids, scores or nuisance thresholds after outcomes
interpreting latent mixture f as empirical sharing prevalence
claiming causal environmental versus geographic separation
claim_ceiling: Synthetic detectability of uncertainty-aware environmental response sharing under fixed sampling support and assumptions. No real flower-colour mechanism, population prevalence, calibrated real-climate power or unbiased global coverage claim. Realistic unknown thresholds, alternative response shapes, phylogenetic dependence and nonuniform independent direction distributions remain untested.
